Translator Browser Release 1.4 and Source Completeness Audit
Status: VERIFIED — COMPLETE INVENTORY AND PHRASE PRESERVATION


The public translator now exposes all 436 indexed senses and all 352 canonical lexical targets through a searchable catalogue. Any English phrase may be entered. Approved semantic material is translated through the canonical pipeline; unfamiliar terms are retained as deterministic EZNAME-0.1 phonemic labels and are never discarded or presented as invented atomic meanings. Strong contextual readings may still resolve automatically, while the whole-phrase coverage view shows canonical options, documented gaps, structural routes, and unfamiliar labels separately.


Every generated lexical performance continues to use the family prefix and opening, full sung carrier, address path, runtime ending, and sentence contour. A self-contained release audit restored and verified all 33 semantic review packets, current gap reports, Gate 4A–4E evidence, Semantic IR, compiler, renderer, glyph/MIDI examples, migrations, and validation reports.


Conversation provenance remains explicit: the original shared conversation contains 313 decoded source nodes and 129 visible speaker turns with SHA-256 5a89af8cda717ce223e252348e0cf2f7735cd2d1f58c7b7655094a3d13862475. This Google document is the integrated human reference; versioned YAML, migrations, review packets, and regression reports remain the machine authority. Current development decisions—English-first input, contextual auto-selection, complete musical playback, phonemic labels, arbitrary-phrase preservation, and full option visibility—are preserved in the repository provenance manifest and Git history.


Validation: 10,938 browser checks, 15 product checks, 11 completeness/provenance checks, and the complete historical regression pass with zero failures. No atomic meaning, address, compact root, carrier, note path, approved compound, or indexed sense route changed.
